exposure: early neuraxial analgesia (less than 3 cm cervical dilation)
late neuraxial analgesia (3 cm cervical dilation or more)
outcome: use of oxytocin for labor augmentation
postpartum hemorrhage of at least 1,000 mL
admission to a neonatal intensive care unit
Apgar scores below 7 at five minutes
cohort: Term multiparous women (at least 37 weeks of gestation) with singleton, cephalic pregnancies and no prior cesarean delivery who gave birth between November 2023 and April 2024.
finding: Among multiparous women, initiating epidural analgesia in early labor was associated with higher rates of labor augmentation and operative delivery compared to late epidural analgesia or no epidural analgesia.
mod_finding: Early neuraxial analgesia was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery (9.80%) and lower rates of spontaneous vaginal delivery (86.27%) compared to late (4.83% cesarean, 95.17% SVD) or no neuraxial analgesia (2.85% cesarean, 96.20% SVD).
